title: Townsend's repelling bismuth raised at Martin
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Townsend's repelling bismuth raised at Martin, about 1950s at Martin Company / Indiana, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: a guy named Townsend discovered that there was a type of bismuth that was repelled instead of attracting.
And he says in this interview with the American Institute of Physics, there's a guy named Townsend [music] who claimed to have uh an isotope of bismuth that repelled instead of attracted.

tellings.link_reason: Both tell Louis Witten's account that Townsend found a bismuth that repelled instead of attracted, raised at Martin.

as_told.title: Louis Witten AIP interview: Townsend Brown's repelling bismuth isotope

plain: The podcast host Jesse Michels points to an interview the physicist Louis Witten gave to the American Institute of Physics, a professional body that records scientists' life stories. Michels says that in it Witten recalls a man named Townsend, linked to the aerospace firm Martin and its research institute known as RIAS in the 1950s, who claimed to have a form of bismuth, a heavy metal, that pushed away instead of pulling. If true, it would mean a defense company heard claims of a material that behaves against normal gravity.
